questions.stem: What makes a hydrocarbon unsaturated?
options: It contains at least one carbon-hydrogen single bond
It contains a halogen atom in place of a hydrogen atom
It contains a ring of carbon atoms joined by single bonds
It contains at least one carbon-carbon double or triple bond
questions.explanation: Unsaturated hydrocarbons, such as alkenes and alkynes, have C=C or C≡C bonds and can add more atoms across them. A ring of single bonds, as in cyclohexane, is still saturated.

questions.stem: Which general formula fits the alkynes with one triple bond?
questions.explanation: Each triple bond removes four hydrogens compared with the alkane, so alkynes are CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ (ethyne is C₂H₂). CₙH₂ₙ fits alkenes and cycloalkanes, and CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ fits alkanes.

questions.stem: A hydrocarbon has the molecular formula C₅H₁₀. Which of these could it be?
questions.explanation: C₅H₁₀ fits CₙH₂ₙ, the formula of both alkenes and cycloalkanes, so it could be cyclopentane (or a pentene). Pentane is C₅H₁₂, and pentyne and cyclopentene are both C₅H₈.

questions.stem: How many hydrogen atoms are in a molecule of nonane, the alkane with 9 carbon atoms?
questions.explanation: Alkanes follow CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, so nonane is C₉H₂₀. 18 would be nonene or cyclononane, and 16 would be nonyne.

questions.stem: Which family of hydrocarbons contains only carbon-carbon single bonds arranged in a ring?
questions.explanation: Cycloalkanes, such as cyclohexane, are rings of carbon atoms joined by single bonds, so they are saturated. Cycloalkenes have a C=C double bond in the ring.

questions.stem: Give the IUPAC name of the unbranched hydrocarbon CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃.
questions.explanation: There are five carbon atoms in an unbranched chain with only single bonds, so the stem is pent- and the ending is -ane. Pentene would need a C=C double bond.

questions.stem: A branched alkane has the condensed formula CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₃. What is its IUPAC name?
questions.explanation: The longest chain has four carbons (butane) with a methyl group on carbon 2 when numbered from the nearer end. Numbering from the other end gives 3-methylbutane, which breaks the lowest-number rule.

questions.stem: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CH=CHCH₃?
questions.explanation: The four-carbon chain has a double bond starting at carbon 2 from either end, so the name is but-2-ene. But-1-ene has the double bond at the end of the chain, CH₂=CHCH₂CH₃.

questions.stem: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CHClCH₃?
questions.explanation: The chain has three carbons with single bonds only (propane) and a chlorine on the middle carbon, carbon 2. 1-chloropropane would have the chlorine on an end carbon, CH₂ClCH₂CH₃.

questions.stem: What is the IUPAC name of HC≡C−CH₃?
questions.explanation: Three carbons give the stem prop-, and the triple bond gives the ending -yne. No locant is needed because the triple bond can only start at carbon 1.

questions.stem: What is the IUPAC name of CH₂=CH−CH(CH₃)−CH₂−CH₃?
questions.explanation: The longest chain containing the double bond has five carbons, numbered from the end nearer the double bond, so it is pent-1-ene with a methyl group on carbon 3. Naming it as a butene with an ethyl branch misses the longest chain.

questions.stem: What is the IUPAC name of CH₂Br−CHBr−CH₂−CH₃?
questions.explanation: The four-carbon saturated chain is butane, with bromine atoms on carbons 1 and 2. The prefix di- shows there are two bromine atoms, and numbering from the left gives the lowest numbers.

questions.stem: What is the structural formula of 2,2-dimethylpropane?
questions.explanation: Propane's middle carbon carries two methyl groups, so it is bonded to four CH₃ groups in total: C(CH₃)₄. CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₃ is 2-methylbutane, an isomer of it.

questions.stem: What is the molecular formula of cyclohexene?
questions.explanation: Cyclohexane is C₆H₁₂; the ring removes two hydrogens compared with hexane. A C=C double bond in the ring removes two more, giving C₆H₁₀.

questions.stem: What are structural isomers?
options: Compounds with the same empirical formula and the same structure
Compounds with the same molecular formula but different structures
Compounds with the same structure but different molecular formulae
Atoms of an element with different numbers of neutrons
questions.explanation: Structural isomers share a molecular formula, such as C₄H₁₀, but their atoms are joined differently, as in butane and 2-methylpropane. Atoms with different numbers of neutrons are isotopes.

questions.stem: How many different alkanes, branched or unbranched, share the molecular formula C₅H₁₂?
questions.explanation: The isomers are pentane, 2-methylbutane and 2,2-dimethylpropane. Structures such as 3-methylbutane are the same molecule as 2-methylbutane drawn from the other end.

questions.stem: How many structural isomers have the molecular formula C₄H₉Cl?
questions.explanation: On a butane chain the chlorine can be on carbon 1 or 2 (1-chlorobutane, 2-chlorobutane). On a 2-methylpropane chain it can be on an end carbon or the central carbon (1-chloro-2-methylpropane, 2-chloro-2-methylpropane), giving 4 in total.

questions.stem: Which pair of compounds are isomers of each other?
questions.explanation: Hex-1-ene and cyclohexane are both C₆H₁₂, with different structures. Hexane is C₆H₁₄ and cyclohexene is C₆H₁₀, so neither matches the formula of its partner.

questions.stem: How many structural isomers have the molecular formula C₂H₄Cl₂?
questions.explanation: The two chlorine atoms can be on the same carbon (1,1-dichloroethane) or on different carbons (1,2-dichloroethane). With only two carbons there is no other arrangement.

questions.stem: What is the empirical formula of butene, C₄H₈?
questions.explanation: The empirical formula is the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms. C₄H₈ divides by 4 to give CH₂; C₂H₄ is still divisible by 2.

questions.stem: What is the empirical formula of hexane, C₆H₁₄?
questions.explanation: 6 and 14 share a highest common factor of 2, so the simplest ratio is C₃H₇. CH₂ would need the H to C ratio to be exactly 2, but in hexane it is 14/6.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes molecular and structural formulae?
options: A molecular formula gives the simplest ratio; a structural formula gives the number of each atom
Both show every bond, but a structural formula also shows the shape of the molecule
A molecular formula gives the number of each atom; a structural formula also shows every bond
A molecular formula shows every bond; a structural formula gives only the simplest ratio
questions.explanation: A molecular formula such as C₂H₆ counts the atoms of each element in one molecule. A structural formula shows all the atoms and how they are bonded; the simplest ratio is the empirical formula.

questions.stem: The boiling points of methane, ethane and propane are −162 °C, −89 °C and −42 °C. What explains the trend?
options: Larger molecules have stronger C−H bonds inside them
Larger molecules are more polar, like water molecules
Larger molecules contain more double bonds
Larger molecules have stronger forces between them
questions.explanation: As the chain gets longer, the intermolecular forces between molecules increase, so more energy is needed to separate them. Boiling does not break C−H bonds, and these alkanes are non-polar with no double bonds.

questions.stem: Pentane boils at 36 °C and 2,2-dimethylpropane at 10 °C, although both are C₅H₁₂. Why is the boiling point of the branched isomer lower?
options: Its compact shape gives less contact, so the forces between molecules are weaker
It has fewer covalent bonds, so less energy is needed to break each molecule apart
It has a lower molar mass, so its molecules move faster at the same temperature
It is more polar, so its molecules repel each other and separate more easily
questions.explanation: Branching makes the molecules more compact, so neighbouring molecules touch over a smaller area and the intermolecular forces are weaker. The isomers have the same molar mass and the same number of bonds, and both are non-polar.

questions.stem: Why are hydrocarbons such as hexane insoluble in water?
options: They are ionic, while water is covalent
They are denser than water and sink to the bottom
They react with water to form new insoluble compounds
They are non-polar, while water is highly polar
questions.explanation: Hydrocarbons are non-polar molecules, so they are not attracted strongly enough to the polar water molecules to mix. Hexane is less dense than water and floats on it.

questions.stem: What is the balanced equation for the complete combustion of propane?
questions.explanation: Complete combustion gives carbon dioxide and water: 3 C give 3CO₂ and 8 H give 4H₂O, needing 6 + 4 = 10 O atoms, or 5O₂. Carbon monoxide forms only with insufficient oxygen.

questions.stem: When butane, C₄H₁₀, burns completely, the balanced equation has 2C₄H₁₀ on the left. What is the coefficient of O₂?
questions.explanation: 2C₄H₁₀ + 13O₂ → 8CO₂ + 10H₂O. The products contain 16 + 10 = 26 O atoms, which is 13O₂; 6.5 is the coefficient for one butane molecule, not two.

questions.stem: Which equation represents the incomplete combustion of methane?
questions.explanation: With insufficient oxygen, methane forms carbon monoxide (or soot) and water, and the equation balances with 3O₂ for every 2CH₄. Forming CO₂ is complete combustion, and hydrogen gas is not a combustion product.

questions.stem: Why is a yellow, sooty flame from a gas heater a safety concern indoors?
options: It shows that hydrogen gas is escaping from the burning fuel
It shows incomplete combustion, which can produce toxic carbon monoxide
It shows complete combustion, which uses up oxygen faster
It shows the fuel is reacting with nitrogen to form toxic gases
questions.explanation: Soot (carbon) in the flame shows there is too little oxygen for complete combustion, and carbon monoxide is also likely to form. Carbon monoxide is colourless and odourless and reduces the blood's ability to carry oxygen.

questions.stem: In sunlight, a mixture of methane and chlorine forms chloromethane and hydrogen chloride. How is this reaction classified?
questions.explanation: A chlorine atom replaces a hydrogen atom: CH₄ + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + HCl. Saturated alkanes react by substitution because there is no double bond to add across.

questions.stem: What are the products when ethane reacts with bromine in ultraviolet light, forming a monosubstituted product?
questions.explanation: Substitution swaps one H for a Br: C₂H₆ + Br₂ → C₂H₅Br + HBr. 1,2-dibromoethane is the addition product of ethene, not a substitution product of ethane.

questions.stem: What is the product when ethene reacts with hydrogen gas over a nickel catalyst?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen adds across the double bond, CH₂=CH₂ + H₂ → CH₃CH₃, converting the alkene into the alkane. This is an addition reaction.

questions.stem: What is the product of the addition reaction between ethene and hydrogen chloride?
questions.explanation: H adds to one carbon and Cl to the other: CH₂=CH₂ + HCl → CH₃CH₂Cl. 1,2-dichloroethane forms when chlorine, Cl₂, adds instead.

questions.stem: Propene, CH₂=CHCH₃, reacts with hydrogen bromide. Which statement about the product is correct?
options: Only bromopropene and hydrogen gas can form
questions.explanation: HBr is asymmetric, so the Br can attach to either carbon of the double bond, giving 1-bromopropane or 2-bromopropane. Addition removes the double bond, so the products are saturated, and dibromo products need Br₂.

questions.stem: How many moles of hydrogen gas are needed to convert 1 mol of propyne completely into propane?
questions.explanation: Propyne has a triple bond, and each mole of H₂ removes one of the extra bonds: HC≡CCH₃ + 2H₂ → CH₃CH₂CH₃. One mole of H₂ would stop at propene.

questions.stem: What is the product when cyclohexene reacts with bromine?
questions.explanation: Br₂ adds across the C=C double bond in the ring, putting a Br on each of the two carbons, and the ring stays intact. Substitution products such as bromocyclohexane form from the saturated cyclohexane in ultraviolet light.

questions.stem: Bromine water is shaken with two colourless liquids in the dark. Liquid A decolourises it immediately; liquid B does not. What can be concluded?
options: Both are alkanes, but A has a longer chain
A is unsaturated and B is saturated
A is saturated and B is unsaturated
A is an alkane and B is an alkene
questions.explanation: Unsaturated compounds add bromine rapidly across their double or triple bonds, removing the orange-brown colour. Saturated compounds do not react with bromine in the dark, so the colour stays.

questions.stem: A student says cyclohexane must decolourise bromine water quickly because it has the same formula as hex-1-ene. Why is the student wrong?
options: Cyclohexane has only single bonds, so it is saturated and does not add bromine
Cyclohexane has a triple bond, so it reacts with bromine only when heated strongly
Cyclohexane and hex-1-ene do not share a formula, as cyclohexane is C₆H₁₀
Cyclohexane is ionic, so it dissolves in water and cannot react with bromine
questions.explanation: Cyclohexane and hex-1-ene are isomers (both C₆H₁₂), but cyclohexane's ring is made of single bonds. With no C=C bond it is saturated, so it gives a negative bromine test, while hex-1-ene decolourises bromine water.
